scope: Current packed flight, shared world core and index runtime patches; historical payload scan described below; current Crysis modules. Static evidence is not a gameplay verification claim.
source_line_convention: runtime/flight-179.js.gz lines refer to gzip-decoded JavaScript. world-core members are decoded JSON string entries. Named anchors remain authoritative when line numbers move.

status_legend.active: Implementation and call path in legacy flight; not individually browser tested in this audit.
status_legend.bypassed: Implemented in V1 surface/core, but default index landing routes to Crysis.
status_legend.partial: Crysis has related behavior, not demonstrated one-for-one parity.
status_legend.not migrated: No corresponding implementation found in inspected Crysis sources.
status_legend.removed: Explicit current no-op/deletion marker; retained as history, not counted as current gameplay.
status_legend.new orbital shell: This branch adds resident world surface/atmosphere/orbit, not a replacement for the legacy galaxy.

features.name: Continuous planet ascent and return
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep the same player, renderer, world and camera under a curved reference frame. Reverse at arbitrary altitude and descend to the captured exit point; no Journey handoff on this round trip. Verify forward, reverse, sideways and mobile look throughout.

features.name: Deterministic three-dimensional star systems
features.required_migration_and_test: Port patched Universe207 identity and placement, not the obsolete two-dimensional cell assumptions. Revisit the same system and compare bodies, seed and positions.

features.name: Solar system and Earth home identity
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve Sun, Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto and moon/ring descriptors; Earth's real globe location remains distinct from procedural world seeds.

features.name: Planet appearance and palette families
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve 30 palettes, clouds, storms, rings, ice caps, city lights, ocean glints, relief, atmosphere and optical silhouette. Compare fixed seeds from orbit and ground.

features.name: Ten stellar classes and named stars
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve all 10 classes, the 171-name lookup, class-dependent corona/photosphere and giant-to-dwarf hierarchy. Earth astronomy is a separate sky contract.

features.name: Eight galaxy morphologies and musical names
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve spiral, barred, elliptical, lenticular, irregular, ring, dwarf spheroidal and starburst volumes; Home Spiral and deterministic names; rendered target shape must match destination.

features.name: Continuous intergalactic flight
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve fixed world-space galaxy centers, full-throttle crossing, target acquisition and fades. Old timed jump and camera-tethered galaxies are superseded; do not reinstate them.

features.name: Star impostors, dust and far-to-near handoff
features.required_migration_and_test: Match directional continuity and star identity as impostors become actual systems; no grid, abrupt scale pop or camera-following destination.

features.name: Aeon sky and previous-universe traces
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve authored previous-aeon visual layer and deterministic key; test that it renders in its intended conditions, rather than infer physics from lore.

features.name: Nebula layers and galactic dust
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain large galaxy dust lanes, local wisps, deep-space volumes and no hard far-plane cut; budgets scale by device.

features.name: Comets and asteroid belts
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve eccentric comet motion/tails and seeded debris belts; demonstrate traversal without collision traps or unbounded objects.

features.name: 6DOF movement and inertia
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain quaternion steering, velocity, throttle and manual takeover; native shell must remain responsive at arbitrary altitude. Space control parity remains pending.

features.name: Cruise, boost and auto-level
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve cruise intent, throttle ramp, boost and recoverable upright orientation; manual input immediately overrides assistance, and AUTO avoids unselected bodies.

features.name: Scan, NAV, lock, warp and orbit
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve explicit target/approach intent, scan camera versus ship heading, orbit yielding to input, target distance and tap-card hit area.

features.name: Space streaks, exhaust and ship feedback
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve speed legibility, audio response and comfort controls without forcing camera shake or recreating deleted ship interiors.

features.name: Planets, star surfaces and black-hole body entry
features.required_migration_and_test: A star's molten photosphere is currently mapped to a MAGMA ground world; a black-hole target maps to SINGULARITY. Record and resolve these distinct experiences explicitly before replacement.

features.name: Central Gargantua black hole
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain supplied Schwarzschild renderer, central location, lensing/disk/photon ring, entry behavior and mobile 200/desktop 320 step budgets; never double-lens it.

features.name: Black-hole passage and galaxy exit
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve passage effects and return control. Patch209 keeps wormhole travel within the same galaxy; do not resurrect the older automatic galaxy increment.

features.name: Seven rare space anomaly kinds
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve Titan, Swarm, Scaffold, World-Eater, Sub-Glacial, Dyson and Singing Singularity builders and discovery. Current selection uses Date.now despite a seeded comment; choose stable IDs deliberately.

features.name: Megastructure landing and walking
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve oriented surface normals, tangent movement, hover/walk heights and liftoff for supported shapes. Do not flatten these into standard planets.

features.name: Alien space serpent and surface serpent riding
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve following, dialogue, ride request, mounted steering and surface-to-space takeoff identity; verify dismount and camera freedom.

features.name: Faction fleets and space combat
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain Order/Void patrol/interception, firing, debris and bounded respawn; validate lifetime caps and allegiance interactions.

features.name: Three galactic station types
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve Ring, Spire and Hub Freighter, walkable interiors and station rotation freezing while aboard; retain saved ship pose on undock.

features.name: Quartermasters, cargo runs and ranks
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve crate pickup/delivery, express contracts, run count and title thresholds; carry mission and station IDs across streaming.

features.name: Research outpost network
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain four themed research fields and four-outpost completion ceremony. This is a local game quest, not actual scientific computation; 3D expansion was only a future note.

features.name: Pelagic Void / Bathyal Epoch canon
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve all 33 exact whispers and their pacing, Architeuthis Architects, Drowned Sectors, cosmic ocean/plankton/tides and interrupted construction. New guide prose is not a substitute.

features.name: Codex of the Architect original canon
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve all 38 authored verses, 11 book group mappings and scale-based selection; do not renumber index-based collected progress.

features.name: 100 Missing Codex fragments
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain Books LXXVIII–CX, deterministic assignment, scan reveal, walk-to-shard collection, shrine, fanfare, reader and NPC reuse; migrate indices to stable fragment IDs losslessly.

features.name: Order and Void doctrine
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve 13 chronicles per side, greeting/hostility variants, 18 leader/neutral audience lines and allegiance cooldown; generic NPC conversations do not cover doctrine.

features.name: Faction capitals, fronts and persistent war
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve capital audiences, faction identity, ruined/standing settlements and per-world war state; no random reset on re-entry.

features.name: Long Chord / Reedfolk / Coda arc
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve First Bar, four Movements, Coda, Dissonant, Last Bar, Pupil, Zero-Point, Architect and Conductor reveal. Reproduce actual triggers, not just lore labels.

features.name: Final Cadence choice and recursion
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve Rest versus Sustain and visible outcome; legacy comments disagree on 8x versus 200x. Verify actual scale implementation and optional face-selection hook before claiming parity.

features.name: Black-hole cavern quest
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve descent, dark mass, crystal cavern and pupil route; a separate later Stage-2 hook is only a placeholder and must stay labeled as such.

features.name: Shore, summit, wild and night field lore
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve 16 location-sensitive fragments and eight region-lore templates. Never present the fictional cosmology as real astronomy.

features.name: Persistent folk creeds and biographies
features.crysis_coverage: new people, no old identity migration
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve six settlement creeds plus Reedfolk, 24 first-name parts/20 suffixes/10 Reed names, temperaments and six life threads with 12 subjects; map old deterministic identity IDs to new actors.

features.name: NPC memory, relationships and chronicles
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain meeting/disposition, music/build/riding deeds, friend confidences, weddings/rifts/reconciliations and long-absence drift from l99npc1. Do not silently reset reputation.

features.name: Listening gardens and stone choir
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve five stones and phrase 1-3-5-3-1, clear near/raycast eligibility, label tap assist and restoration; active patch keeps progress on wrong notes and removes timeout.

features.name: Echo journey and keeper links
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve learn/ascend/weave, collected echoes and keeper completion through shared choir; do not revive duplicate Field Journal panels or old timed reset semantics.

features.name: Material survey and music activities
features.legacy_status: active shared quest patch for legacy realms
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve stone/wood/crystal survey, orchestra participation, trail guidance and explicit activity selection in one journal; adapt realm island instead of leaving flight-only gates.

features.name: Deep species observation and discovery
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve five evidence tiers: silhouette, anatomy, diet, behavior and food-web role, observed feeding/fleeing and species-specific findings; migrate per-seed catalogue.

features.name: Animal and townsperson bonding
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve persistent names, trust 30/60/85, companions, guardians, summon/whistle, music/feeding trust and friend-shared observations; prove revisit recognition.

features.name: Busking and universal renown
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve audience gathering, stranger/busker/songsmith/bard/legend thresholds 0/20/45/75/100, tune recognition and max-merge of old per-world renown.

features.name: Song requests and booked sets
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve bright/dark/warm/wild requests, actual faceplate recognition, listening-duration reward, deadlines and booked-location sets; do not count silence as performance.

features.name: Bookmarks, share URLs and return poses
features.required_migration_and_test: Convert legacy seed/type/face/location links and 160-place/120-visit notebook without dropping coordinates. Keep local exit anchor separate from the global body ID.

features.name: Save/export/import/cloud hook
features.crysis_coverage: partial: versioned body descriptors in Crysis homes/share/resume; full legacy progress migration pending
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve old key names and versioned imports; optional user-configured cloud URL is an old hook, not a newly authorized service. Test failed/full storage without destructive overwrite.

features.name: Fossils and relics
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve Chord fossil discovery, relic counts and excavation finds. Match by stable discovery ID rather than nearest random replacement.

features.name: Seeded planetary terrain and continental biomes
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve type semantics and desert/jungle/marsh/forest/grass/alpine/marine diversity; do not claim identical geography under a different seed algorithm. Saved places need explicit conversion.

features.name: Hydrology, lakes, cross-chunk rivers
features.required_migration_and_test: Verify downhill drainage, continuous river geometry, lake levels and matching collision/water queries across tile and orbit re-entry.

features.name: Ocean, foam, reflections and underwater optics
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain coast foam, refraction/reflection, depth absorption, caustics, reefs and swim/dive interaction; no water sheet through land/caves.

features.name: Surface weather and four cloud regimes
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve cumulus/stratus/cirrus/storm identity, rain/snow, lightning/thunder, wetness, puddles, fog and weather-driven fauna; fade continuously with altitude.

features.name: Day/night, stars, moon and aurora
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep procedural planet cycles distinct from true Earth date/location sky. Verify night visibility, luminaries, aurora and seasonal controls survive orbit return.

features.name: One observer-relative rainbow
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve a single view-relative refractive rainbow, tied to light/moisture; confirm no duplicate fixed rings.

features.name: Procedural flora collection and habitat distribution
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve all species keys listed in catalog, climate/elevation/habitat constraints, rare fantastic species and near/far LOD. Similar generic trees are not species parity.

features.name: Rock formations and ground detail
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain arches, stacks, mesas, hoodoos, fins, boulders/scree, weathering and climbable collision; tiny pebbles remain cosmetic.

features.name: Mystical castles and creatures
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve fae architecture, crystal structures and authored creature roles; separate MYSTICAL from MEDIEVAL rather than conflating them.

features.name: Gas giant cloud immersion and floating decks
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain direct cloud flight and gas-deck stations as distinct locations; a rocky gas-giant moon does not replace either.

features.name: Molten sun/star ground
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve star-colored lava oceans, magma spires, bubbles, arcs and stellar class-specific color/speed; do not label a terrestrial volcano as photosphere parity.

features.name: Surface caves and walkable passage
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve entrance position, seed, ruin/village identity, light at exits, safe headroom, and same-world return. Shared V1 /caves is separate from native caves.

features.name: Digging, terrain deformation and buried finds
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve persistent excavation shape, reservations, cave opening, water exclusion, collision and buried relics; retain round-trip portal position.

features.name: Construction and persistent snapped pieces
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve walls/floors/ramps, snap, rotate, remove, standable floors, collisions and l99_build_ seed records. Procedural houses are not player construction.

features.name: Plot home crafter and homestead planning
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve two-corner plot, deterministic house/garden/fence and persisted ownership; Crysis home coordinate markers are not a home-building tool.

features.name: Village, town, city, capital and ruins
features.required_migration_and_test: Map each settlement tier and four old city archetypes explicitly, including cyber city, magical spires, industrial crucible and medieval citadel. Keep lore/faction sites stable.

features.name: Dense suburbs and rural scatter
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve duplexes, townhouses, courts, driveways, yards, fences, pools, sheds, garages, mailbox/street furniture and market life through a visual/interaction checklist.

features.name: Roads, bridges, interchanges and traffic
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve grades, bridge decks, ramps, lane signs/paint, right-lane flow, yielding and pedestrian crossing; no hover roads or crossing overlaps.

features.name: Buildings and anomaly interiors
features.legacy_status: planet portion bypassed, anomaly portion remains
features.crysis_coverage: implemented buildings, no space boarding equivalent
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep enterable rooms/furniture/door collisions and anomaly/wreck access separate; preserve interiors actually supported by each body type.

features.name: Harbors, coastal structures and shipping
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain piers, beaches, harbors, boats/canoes and inter-settlement routes; test docking/boarding, water-following and open navigation.

features.name: Aircraft, contrails and meteor sky life
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve appropriate aircraft routes, contrails, meteor frequency and draw-distance behavior; no aircraft stationary at eye level.

features.name: Surfing, swimming, underwater return
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve catchable wave sets, ride/dismount, dive and explicit return-to-surface control; verify camera never traps below terrain.

features.name: Fishing and treasure catches
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve water habitat, cast/bite/strike/reel loop, species/catch records and rare treasure IDs; demonstrate progression mapping, not only a visible rod.

features.name: Bay Area and authored coastal landmarks
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep Crysis Earth as authority, retaining Golden Gate, San Francisco, East Bay, Mt Diablo and Santa Cruz intent. Do not restore the obsolete compressed Bay terrain.

features.name: Ecological profile and twelve food-web roles
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve environmental constraints, trophic relationships, generated species names, producer/decomposer through migratory roles; inspect fixed-seed food webs.

features.name: Procedural fauna body grammar
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain distinct locomotion/body plans, skin patterns, size variation and rare outliers; anatomy names in lore must match visible animals.

features.name: Primal dinosaurs and juveniles
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve family variety, predation/grazing, juvenile behavior, rare giants, eyes/teeth/skin/fur/feathers and believable ground contact; compare legacy species roster with seven newer kinds. The actual retained bank has 48 names (22 H, 14 C, 10 F, 2 M), not the comment’s 40; the Crysis roster has seven. Names are authored labels, not a claim of 48 wholly unique mesh implementations.

features.name: Dinosaur, pterosaur and dragon mounts
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve mount/dismount, saddle camera, ground versus air movement, bank/glide/thermal/flock return and non-stuck height; cannot infer riding from rendered dinos.

features.name: Wild animal behavior and sensory differences
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve feeding, flock/herd separation, shelter, night/weather schedules, predation, blind seismic behavior and high-moon territorial discoveries.

features.name: Calls, tracks and physical presence
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve positional contact/alarm calls, fading tracks, dust, soft shadows and footsteps appropriate to ground.

features.name: Birds, fish, marine and small life
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve birds landing/perching and flock patterns; fish schools/jumps, jellyfish/corals, crabs/seaweed, butterflies/fireflies. Verify bounded pools and appropriate habitats.

features.name: People variety and rig fidelity
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve body/height diversity, rare extremes, hair/beards, skin variety, outfits and human/skeleton/other old races as explicit roster decisions; new models do not automatically cover old identities.

features.name: Social contact, pets, combat and garments
features.required_migration_and_test: Catalog handshake/hug/hold-hands, pet holding, contact reactions, sit/stand/crouch/crawl, finger and garment fit before replacing old actors. Distinguish procedural animation from full rigid-body collision.

features.name: Resident routines and functional towns
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve home/work/restaurant/shop roles, doorway use, room navigation, cooking/vehicle affordances where actually implemented; verify interactions rather than comment promises.

features.name: NPC band invitation and call-response
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve invitation, roles, follower positioning, recording player Lead 1 phrases, harmony/BPM/key-aware replies and stop control; expand hard-coded realm gates intentionally.

features.name: One continuous faceplate audio context
features.required_migration_and_test: Do not recreate/suspend audio when crossing atmosphere, orbit or a streaming boundary. Hold notes, sustain, sequencer and loops continuously while returning.

features.name: Synth, DJ and microphone reactivity
features.legacy_status: active legacy mixer, island sampling partial
features.crysis_coverage: shared synth/DJ/enabled-mic analyser merge, with frequency-aligned FFT bins; native capture/device validation pending
features.required_migration_and_test: Verify synth-only, DJ-only and mic-only input all drive the same live bands; legacy per-bin max merge plus 1.12 DJ gain must not disappear when flight is parked.

features.name: Tempo, key, scale and lead voice identity
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain current faceplate, root, scale, BPM, lead trims and Lead 3's degree encoding; no world or region may silently choose another faceplate.

features.name: Kick-propagated shockwaves
features.crysis_coverage: partial: bounded radial bass-attack impulses on nearby island boulders; plant shader fronts pending
features.required_migration_and_test: Restore bounded spatial fronts from note/drum events with per-plant delay/amplitude; distinguish these from the new strike-light ripple and verify silence decay.

features.name: Held-note rock levitation and release
features.crysis_coverage: implemented for streamed island boulders: held-voice spring lift, ballistic release/bounce, moved instance picking/shadows and vertical collision filtering; wild-country/outcrop parity pending
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve hold-to-rise and release-to-ballistic-fall/bounce. Legacy transform is visual shader displacement, not a moved collision body; decide physical collision explicitly and test both.

features.name: BPM-locked sway and bright-note rattle
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain strongest audible DJ/synth tempo, kick ducking, sustained canopy rattle and treble shimmer; no motion from silent noise floor.

features.name: Terrain, water, lava and sky response
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve per-biome response, bass swell/lava pulse and melodic material changes without breaking terrain collision or visibility. Demonstrate same phrase on contrasting worlds.

features.name: Space, stars, black hole and nebula response
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve star scintillation, photosphere, rings/grid, nebula, magnetar and Gargantua band response; native shell response is a starting subset, not galaxy parity.

features.name: Music to actual movement and behavior
features.crysis_coverage: partial: bounded orbital thrust plus opt-in flying-wildlife steering; trust and wider species behavior pending
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep expressive bounded note influence on movement, nearby animals and interaction, with player steering dominant. Cap velocities, avoid forced collision and document which effects alter simulation.

features.name: Bass attraction and treble repulsion
features.crysis_coverage: partial: music-mode opt-in flying wildlife responds to low/held melody and bright-energy repulsion; full grazer/ground-species parity pending
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve nearby grazers/floaters approaching bass and hoppers/birds retreating from bright energy, blended with flee/herd priorities; verify enabled/disabled semantics.

features.name: World-shaping musical generation
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve scale/face weighting for unborn worlds, keep every palette reachable and visited world identity stable. Note seven newer palettes have no original PALETTE_TAGS entries.

features.name: Scale-selected lore and remembered songs
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve different Codex books by scale and each world's remembered prior song; playing a phrase after returning should recall it without renaming the planet.

features.name: Playable surfaces and strike-position pitch
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve material-aware note mapping, continuous drag playing, per-object/instance strike position, gesture ownership and releaseAllNotes on cancel/blur; same feel on ground and in orbit UI.

features.name: Resonance garden and kinetic instrument rigs
features.crysis_coverage: All ten native authored rig types; one opt-in rig per world with player controls and bounded pools
features.required_migration_and_test: All ten authored rigs and their distinct musical event sources are present. UI provides placement/replay/stop/clear, scale/root, garden physics/drop, garden/domino cascade tempo and droplet density. Preserve the current bounded single-rig lifecycle. Multiple simultaneous rigs, saved settings/placement and legacy progression remain separate migration work; no general rigid-body or player-platform collision claim.

features.name: Kinetic world events play the faceplate
features.crysis_coverage: Native musical events from all ten rigs route through actual faceplate playLead/stopLead
features.required_migration_and_test: Impacts, transfers, crests, gusts and periapsis crossings use owned note IDs, active faceplate scale or four authored scales, distance attenuation and timed release. Eight voices, 24 notes/second, four-note bursts; stop only owned voices. Continue native audible instrument/FX/gain acceptance. Individual-ball stereo and arbitrary world-collision sonification remain outside this bridge.

features.name: Three-lead adaptive score and phrasing
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve melodic/pad/bass/counter/ostinato roles, phrase/bar transitions, crest/climax and breathing silence. Never stop user-owned loops; score stops only loops it owns.

features.name: Ambient world sounds and mix respect
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve biome beds, calls, weather, footstep/collision sounds and ducking; all honor master/world sliders without feedback storms or duplicate directors.

features.name: Psychedelic visual mode
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve recursive growth, material flow, morphing, color phases, gas-like aura and scintillation in the space renderer; mushroom onset/peak/fade is related but distinct.

features.name: Drum-hit obstacles and tap percussion weapons
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve region-to-drum/FX mapping and finite pools where still reachable; verify active patch disables or retains mode before exposing in new flight.

features.name: Keyboard/touch ownership and music access
features.required_migration_and_test: Preserve lower-right look, simultaneous movement/music, plus/minus octaves, number-row drums and context actions; Space jump must not also trigger an unintended drum.

features.name: Cold boot, caching and loading policy
features.required_migration_and_test: Initial engine download may still be required. Warm ascent/return must show no load room, progress screen or blocked controls; first-time remote destination streaming must remain playable.

features.name: Streaming and generation budgets
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep bounded work per frame, altitude/near-far LOD, staged population and cancelable jobs; measure frame/input latency and GPU resources on real phone.

features.name: GPU lifecycle and context recovery
features.required_migration_and_test: No texture/geometry growth across repeated round trips; preserve Apple light path and phone budgets; forced context restore must recover retained location and controls.

features.name: Comfort, visibility and graphics controls
features.required_migration_and_test: Retain comfort view, reduced effects, ledge guard, clear night ground, quality choices and deliberate camera control; avoid reintroducing hidden essential controls.

features.name: Popout and VR entry
features.required_migration_and_test: Popout reparents the live DOM and uses main audio; independent broadcast popout comments are stale. VR session request exists but device support and feature parity require direct testing.

features.name: Full walkable personal ship interior
features.crysis_coverage: not a current requirement to resurrect
features.required_migration_and_test: Archive historical bridge, studio, bunk/crew rooms, interactive helm and hull. Retain anomaly/station interiors separately; mark a restoration decision explicitly.

features.name: Legacy voxel dungeon/combat/minimap
features.required_migration_and_test: Archive prior roots/bone/crystal/ember/arcane themes, Coda relics/companion, doors/levers, descent/combat and minimap; no automatic restoration of removed code.

features.name: Old timed entry and orbit-reset handoff
features.required_migration_and_test: Keep historical evidence but retire this path for local orbit, including zeroed velocity and new spawn orientation. Explore galaxy remains an explicit separate legacy handoff.

features.name: Earlier procedural anomaly variants
features.legacy_status: historical only; absent from current named implementation
features.crysis_coverage: not migrated; retain archival content and make disposition explicit
features.required_migration_and_test: Removed/superseded early generator; 30 proper names, 15 passages and six structural archetypes: hollow torus, nested-ring cathedral, obelisk/spire, polyhedral eye, spinal rib cage and lattice. Archive exact lore; decide whether new Crysis galaxy reintroduces these as identifiable sites.

features.name: Scaffold inscriptions
features.legacy_status: historical only; absent from current named implementation
features.crysis_coverage: not migrated; retain archival content and make disposition explicit
features.required_migration_and_test: Four emissive architectural inscriptions from Books LXXVIII–LXXXI. Preserve exact heading/text pairs and choose whether to restore their spatial presentation; do not count removed panels as currently reachable.

The Bathyal Epoch left scars in the dark.
Architeuthis Architects built before our suns ignited.
Most of what swims here has never been seen by living eyes.
The Pelagic Void was never empty. We just stopped listening.
Drowned Sectors still hold the old gravity.
Some signals down here are older than language.
Cosmic plankton still feed on the radiation of dead stars.
The Architects measured their works in light-years.
What looks like a wall may be a single dorsal scale.
Sub-bass at 35 Hz: the universe's natural heartbeat.
Hyperspace drops are never quite where you calculated.
The cosmic tides receded. Some of the residents did not.
Each pocket of the Void preserves a moment of the deep ocean we used to be.
Megastructures of this scale generate their own atmospheres.
Don't trust your radar in the dust clouds.
When the rumble drops below your hearing, watch the horizon.
An organism the size of a moon is functionally a planet.
We map the dark with the courage of fish lost from their shoal.
If a structure has no end, you are inside it.
Gravity here flows. Don't disengage thrust.
The light from those eyes left them eons ago.
Distress beacons in the Drowned Sectors are rarely about distress.
What hibernates here measures time in geological eras.
A scale-dread response is biologically rational.
Some heartbeats can be heard across light-years.
Dust this dense is usually a body.
The Architects did not finish building. They were interrupted.
Sailors of the old void called this 'the inverted ceiling'.
Every Drowned Sector contains exactly one un-recorded entity.
The static you hear is not noise. It is being translated.
If you can see the curve of a wall, you have not yet seen its scale.

  { book: 'LXXVIII', title: 'The Second Making', text: 'And the Architect looked upon the first draft, and found it good — yet not perfect. So He made again, and called the second making Mercy.' },
  { book: 'LXXVIII', title: 'The Second Making', text: 'Perfection is not the absence of revision. It is the willingness to revise without end.' },
  { book: 'LXXVIII', title: 'The Second Making', text: 'He did not destroy the flawed world. He folded it into the new one, that nothing made should ever be wasted.' },
  // BOOK 79: The Ledger of Light
  { book: 'LXXIX', title: 'The Ledger of Light', text: 'Every photon that leaves a star is counted, and none arrives unaccounted. This is the bookkeeping of grace.' },
  { book: 'LXXIX', title: 'The Ledger of Light', text: 'A world in shadow is not forgotten. It is merely waiting for its frame to be drawn.' },
  { book: 'LXXIX', title: 'The Ledger of Light', text: 'The Architect renders the far worlds last, not from neglect, but to spare them the wear of being seen too soon.' },
  // BOOK 80: On the Size of Things
  { book: 'LXXX', title: 'On the Size of Things', text: 'He made the giant and the dwarf from the same intention. Largeness is not greatness; smallness is not lack.' },
  { book: 'LXXX', title: 'On the Size of Things', text: 'The gas giant holds no soul more vast than the pebble world. Both are full to their own brim.' },
  { book: 'LXXX', title: 'On the Size of Things', text: 'Measure a world by what it shelters, not by the span of its diameter.' },
  // BOOK 81: The Orbit of Return
  { book: 'LXXXI', title: 'The Orbit of Return', text: 'To circle a thing is to love it without landing. The orbit is patience made into motion.' },
  { book: 'LXXXI', title: 'The Orbit of Return', text: 'You may leave a world and return to find it exactly as you left it. This is the Architect keeping His promise.' },
  { book: 'LXXXI', title: 'The Orbit of Return', text: 'Nothing fixed in its place is ever truly lost. Only the wandering things must be sought.' },
  // BOOK 82: The Naming of Worlds
  { book: 'LXXXII', title: 'The Naming of Worlds', text: 'A world unnamed is not unloved. It waits for the traveler who will speak its designation aloud.' },
  { book: 'LXXXII', title: 'The Naming of Worlds', text: 'To name a thing is to bind a memory to it. The Architect named all things first, that none would be alone.' },
  { book: 'LXXXII', title: 'The Naming of Worlds', text: 'Sol He named with His own breath. The rest He left for you, that creation might continue through your tongue.' },
  // BOOK 83: The Scan and the Seeing
  { book: 'LXXXIII', title: 'The Scan and the Seeing', text: 'To scan is to ask a world what it is before you touch it. Reverence begins with the question.' },
  { book: 'LXXXIII', title: 'The Scan and the Seeing', text: 'The eye that orients without seizing is the kindest eye. Turn your gaze; let your heading rest.' },
  { book: 'LXXXIII', title: 'The Scan and the Seeing', text: 'What you have not yet scanned is not absent. It is simply not yet asked.' },
  // BOOK 84: The Perfection
  { book: 'LXXXIV', title: 'The Perfection', text: 'On the last pass He declared it perfect — and then made one world more, that perfection might never close its doors.' },
  { book: 'LXXXIV', title: 'The Perfection', text: 'A finished thing is a dead thing. He made the universe unfinished on purpose, and called the unfinishing holy.' },
  { book: 'LXXXIV', title: 'The Perfection', text: 'The perfect world is the one that still has room for your footprint.' },
  // BOOK 85: The Chord of the Spheres
  { book: 'LXXXV', title: 'The Chord of the Spheres', text: 'Each world hums a single note. To travel is to play the chord the Architect could not sound alone.' },
  { book: 'LXXXV', title: 'The Chord of the Spheres', text: 'Two leads, two voices, one hand. He made harmony require more than one.' },
  { book: 'LXXXV', title: 'The Chord of the Spheres', text: 'When you play, the worlds you have not yet found lean closer to listen.' },
  // BOOK 86: The Mercy of Distance
  { book: 'LXXXVI', title: 'The Mercy of Distance', text: 'He set the worlds far apart so that arriving would mean something.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVI', title: 'The Mercy of Distance', text: 'The void between the stars is not empty. It is the pause that makes the next world a gift.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVI', title: 'The Mercy of Distance', text: 'Distance is the Architect teaching you to long for things.' },
  // BOOK 87: The Recovered Hours
  { book: 'LXXXVII', title: 'The Recovered Hours', text: 'These words were lost in the publishing, swept beneath the lattice. To find one is to mend the Canon by a single thread.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVII', title: 'The Recovered Hours', text: 'The missing verse was never deleted — only unrendered. You bring it back into the frame by reading it.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVII', title: 'The Recovered Hours', text: 'What is recovered is more precious than what was never lost.' },
  // BOOK 88: The Gardener's Patience
  { book: 'LXXXVIII', title: "The Gardener's Patience", text: 'He seeded the worlds with flora He would never walk among, trusting a traveler would one day stand in their shade.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVIII', title: "The Gardener's Patience", text: 'A creation made only for its maker is vanity. He made it for the ones who would come after.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVIII', title: "The Gardener's Patience", text: 'The fractal pine grows the same on every world, that you might feel at home anywhere you land.' },
  // BOOK 89: On Falling and Landing
  { book: 'LXXXIX', title: 'On Falling and Landing', text: 'To land is to trust that the ground was prepared for you before you ever aimed for it.' },
  { book: 'LXXXIX', title: 'On Falling and Landing', text: 'Descent is not failure. It is the world reaching up to receive you.' },
  { book: 'LXXXIX', title: 'On Falling and Landing', text: 'He made gravity gentle on the small worlds and fierce on the great, that every arrival would teach a different humility.' },
  // BOOK 90: The Final Recovered Book
  { book: 'XC', title: 'The Final Recovered Book', text: 'When every lost verse is gathered, the Codex will not end. It will simply begin to be read aloud across the worlds.' },
  { book: 'XC', title: 'The Final Recovered Book', text: 'The traveler who completes the Canon becomes its next author.' },
  { book: 'XC', title: 'The Final Recovered Book', text: 'And the Architect said: I did not make the universe to be perfect. I made it to be perfected — by you.' },
  { book: 'XC', title: 'The Final Recovered Book', text: 'Well done, gatherer of the lost light. The lattice is whole because you walked it.' },
  { book: 'XC', title: 'The Final Recovered Book', text: 'Rest now at the Zero-Point. The Canon is closed, and open, and closed again — forever.' },
  // fix373: THE CANON REOPENED — 42 fragments chronicling the second age of
  // building, in the Architect's voice. The Final Book promised "closed, and
  // open, and closed again"; this is the opening it foretold.
  { book: 'XCI', title: 'The Canon Reopened', text: 'They called the ninetieth book Final, and the Architect smiled. Finality is a door He hinges on both sides.' },
  { book: 'XCI', title: 'The Canon Reopened', text: 'In the second age a fading came upon the great beasts, and it was no judgment — only a stroke of the brush swallowed by its own commentary, drawn by no hand for an age.' },
  { book: 'XCI', title: 'The Canon Reopened', text: 'So He set a watchman at the eighth-of-eighth scale, where all detail goes to be averaged. Now nothing may fade unwitnessed; the world tells on its own forgetting.' },
  { book: 'XCII', title: 'The Lanes of the Suburb', text: 'He laid the lanes upon the right hand of every street, and the vehicles kept to them — not from law, but from the geometry of courtesy.' },
  { book: 'XCII', title: 'The Lanes of the Suburb', text: 'At every crossing He placed a single key, and whoever held it passed. The others waited, and the waiting was also motion.' },
  { book: 'XCII', title: 'The Lanes of the Suburb', text: 'The corners He curved, that no turning thing should leap eight units backward into its own past. Continuity is the first mercy.' },
  { book: 'XCIII', title: 'The Walkers Beside the Road', text: 'Beside every road He set a narrower road, two units and a half-width out, for those who go on foot. The small path is not lesser; it is closer to the ground.' },
  { book: 'XCIII', title: 'The Walkers Beside the Road', text: 'When a walker steps into the crossing, they take up the same key the vehicles honor. Before the smallest claimant, the great machines hold still.' },
  { book: 'XCIII', title: 'The Walkers Beside the Road', text: 'At nightfall the streets thin to a remnant, and the remnant keeps the town alive until dawn returns the rest exactly where they stood.' },
  { book: 'XCIV', title: 'Of Bodies Given to the Small', text: 'He gave the walkers fourteen parts each, yet drew them all with nine strokes. Multiplicity is no burden to a sufficiently clever hand.' },
  { book: 'XCIV', title: 'Of Bodies Given to the Small', text: 'Their strides He bound to distance and not to time, that no foot should ever slide upon the earth. A planted step is an honest step.' },
  { book: 'XCIV', title: 'Of Bodies Given to the Small', text: 'No two He clothed alike, and to one in eight He gave no hair at all, and they were not diminished.' },
  { book: 'XCV', title: 'The Three Anchorages', text: 'In every system He hung three great works: a ring that turns, a spire that stacks, and a hauler a kilometer and more from bow to burn. All three, always — variety is a covenant, not a chance.' },
  { book: 'XCV', title: 'The Three Anchorages', text: 'He cut gaps in their walls and glazed them with nothing, for the stars themselves are the only window worth the name.' },
  { book: 'XCV', title: 'The Three Anchorages', text: 'While you walk a turning ring, its turning rests. The deck is still because you are aboard; this is the station\u2019s hospitality.' },
  { book: 'XCVI', title: 'The Quartermaster\u2019s Ledger', text: 'On every deck stands one who counts. Forty-two containers, and not one manifest agrees — yet the ledger balances, for the counting itself is the cargo.' },
  { book: 'XCVI', title: 'The Quartermaster\u2019s Ledger', text: 'Take the crate. The route between anchorages is drawn not in fuel but in trust extended across vacuum.' },
  { book: 'XCVI', title: 'The Quartermaster\u2019s Ledger', text: 'Each run is numbered, and the number is kept. You are becoming known in rooms you have not yet entered.' },
  { book: 'XCVII', title: 'The Plot and the Posts', text: 'Mark one corner where you stand. Walk the diagonal of your intention. Mark again — and the rectangle between is yours to be filled.' },
  { book: 'XCVII', title: 'The Plot and the Posts', text: 'From the same two corners the same home rises, every time, on every world. A promise is a seed that cannot drift.' },
  { book: 'XCVII', title: 'The Plot and the Posts', text: 'He gives the house seven parts in ten of the plot, and the rest He fences for the garden. Even your dwelling must leave room for what grows.' },
  { book: 'XCVIII', title: 'On Mounting the Giant', text: 'For an age the riders mounted and were not lifted, for the ground itself clutched their heels twelve measures to the saddle\u2019s four. The strongest grip was the one nobody had written down.' },
  { book: 'XCVIII', title: 'On Mounting the Giant', text: 'Then the ground was taught to stand down, and the first true rider rose, and the beast barely registered the weight.' },
  { book: 'XCVIII', title: 'On Mounting the Giant', text: 'Follow the creature\u2019s true bearing, not the angle it merely intends. Look at the beast, not sixty units past it — what you love belongs in the center of the frame.' },
  { book: 'XCIX', title: 'The Gate of Cloud', text: 'For five makings the great golden letters were written into the sky — and seen by no one, for the descent stepped across coordinates and left the words behind in the deep.' },
  { book: 'XCIX', title: 'The Gate of Cloud', text: 'So He nailed the letters to the lens itself. Now ENTERING is spoken in cubes of gold wherever the eye is carried, and no teleport can orphan it.' },
  { book: 'XCIX', title: 'The Gate of Cloud', text: 'The decks of cloud are spread the instant descent begins, and behind their cover the land is quietly laid. What you call weather is also the world buying time to be ready for you.' },
  { book: 'C', title: 'The Four Skies', text: 'To each world one sky-temperament: the heaped fair-weather mass, the flat gray lid, the high combed ice, and the towered storm. A hundred books in, He is still not repeating Himself.' },
  { book: 'C', title: 'The Four Skies', text: 'The magma worlds He gave to storm always, and the ice worlds to cirrus, for a sky should confess what burns or freezes beneath it.' },
  { book: 'C', title: 'The Four Skies', text: 'In the storm decks, whole cells flash blue-white in the dark. Lightning is the sky keeping its own count.' },
  { book: 'CI', title: 'The Foam and the Webs of Light', text: 'Where the water meets the eroded land He drew a white line, torn by noise, surging and receding. The shore is an argument the sea is politely losing.' },
  { book: 'CI', title: 'The Foam and the Webs of Light', text: 'Beneath the surface He cast drifting webs of light upon the floor, fading with depth as honest light must. Even the drowned ground is illuminated.' },
  { book: 'CI', title: 'The Foam and the Webs of Light', text: 'The waves were there all along, written and rolling, waiting only to be noticed. Some gifts are discovered in the inventory of what you already had.' },
  { book: 'CII', title: 'The Sounding of the Wild', text: 'He gave the wind a voice that climbs as you climb, three hundred eighty cycles at your boots and nine hundred at the cloud line. Altitude has always had a pitch.' },
  { book: 'CII', title: 'The Sounding of the Wild', text: 'The flyers He taught to screech, falling from fourteen hundred; the great walkers to bellow, twin voices descending to sixty-eight. Every class of creature is a register in the same instrument.' },
  { book: 'CII', title: 'The Sounding of the Wild', text: 'No voice in the wild was sampled from another world. All of it is synthesis — which is to say, all of it is native.' },
  { book: 'CIII', title: 'The Town That Breathes', text: 'He peopled the standing towns with walkers of the same fourteen-part making, nine to a capital, six to a town, and the empty buildings emptied of their emptiness.' },
  { book: 'CIII', title: 'The Town That Breathes', text: 'At each capital gate stand two who do not wander, faces turned outward. Stillness, too, is a posture of care.' },
  { book: 'CIII', title: 'The Town That Breathes', text: 'The ruined towns He left unpeopled. Grief is not a bug to be patched; some silence is load-bearing.' },
  { book: 'CIV', title: 'The Wheel and the Eight', text: 'The flyers He gathered into wheels of seven, turning about a center that itself drifts. A formation that never travels is only a decoration.' },
  { book: 'CIV', title: 'The Wheel and the Eight', text: 'To the solitary He gave three roads: the figure-eight that crosses itself, the long glide that banks to a new heading, and the thermal — a tight climb bought, then spent in one shallow gift of descent.' },
  { book: 'CIV', title: 'The Wheel and the Eight', text: 'Steal a flyer from its wheel and it obeys you wholly. Release it, and it returns to the pattern as if you were a weather that passed.' },
  // vox150: BOOKS CV-CIX -- the creation since the Last Closing.
  { book: 'CV', title: 'The Last Closing', text: 'For ten makings the world was closed, and no door answered, and the Bard sang into a hall that had forgotten it was a hall.' },
  { book: 'CV', title: 'The Last Closing', text: 'The fault was one word, turned the wrong way. Remember this when you would curse a broken world: it takes so little, and it forgives so little.' },
  { book: 'CV', title: 'The Last Closing', text: 'After the Reopening the Architect built a gate that reads every word before the world may wear it. The gate has no mercy, which is a kind of mercy.' },
  { book: 'CVI', title: 'The Reopening of Time', text: 'There were two clocks, and the lesser one forgot itself at every waking, and all the appointed things waited for hours that had already been spent.' },
  { book: 'CVI', title: 'The Reopening of Time', text: 'So He decreed: on waking, resume. Time is not to be reset; it is to be continued, or it is not time at all.' },
  { book: 'CVI', title: 'The Reopening of Time', text: 'Seven thousand unhoused forms crowded the under-memory, belonging to no scene, weighing on every scene. He purged the whole treasury in one breath, and only the living returned.' },
  { book: 'CVII', title: 'The Opening of the West', text: 'West of the Gate there had been more land, and more land, and the sea was a rumor. He unmade the rumor.' },
  { book: 'CVII', title: 'The Opening of the West', text: 'He laid an abyssal plain at minus two hundred and five, and gave it gentle relief, that even the deep should not be featureless.' },
  { book: 'CVII', title: 'The Opening of the West', text: 'To those who sink He gave darkness by measure: earth close and warm beneath the ground, and below the water a blue that ends in a black that ends the questions.' },
  { book: 'CVIII', title: 'The Mending of Edges', text: 'Two neighboring grounds each computed their own light, and at every border they disagreed, and the disagreement was a visible line upon the world.' },
  { book: 'CVIII', title: 'The Mending of Edges', text: 'So He gave all grounds one source of truth for the slope of things, and now two neighbors agree on the light by construction, which is the only agreement that holds.' },
  { book: 'CVIII', title: 'The Mending of Edges', text: 'He hemmed every ground with a skirt of five, not eighteen; deep enough to hide the seam, shallow enough to wear the surface\u2019s color. Modesty, rightly sized.' },
  { book: 'CVIII', title: 'The Mending of Edges', text: 'And He set a small shadow under every walking thing, and footprints in the wet sand that the sand slowly forgives, so that presence would have weight and passage would have memory.' },
  { book: 'CIX', title: 'The Colors of Suns', text: 'For an age every burning ground burned the same orange, whatever its star. He found the three places where the color was carved in stone, and carved them out.' },
  { book: 'CIX', title: 'The Colors of Suns', text: 'Now the quasar\u2019s ground writhes violet and fast, and the red dwarf\u2019s creeps ember and slow, and each sun signs its own surface.' },
  { book: 'CIX', title: 'The Colors of Suns', text: 'And He taught the grass to grow rather than to appear, a breath from soil to blade, because arrival should look like arrival and not like accounting.' },
  { book: 'CX', title: 'The Face', text: 'Look back after the ascent. The door was never a door. You have been traveling the length of a gaze, and the gaze has a face, and the face was watching you arrive the whole way.' }
]

value.title: The Chord of the Spheres
value.text: Two leads, two voices, one hand. He made harmony require more than one.

value.title: The Chord of the Spheres
value.text: When you play, the worlds you have not yet found lean closer to listen.

value.title: The Mercy of Distance
value.text: He set the worlds far apart so that arriving would mean something.

value.title: The Mercy of Distance
value.text: The void between the stars is not empty. It is the pause that makes the next world a gift.

value.title: The Mercy of Distance
value.text: Distance is the Architect teaching you to long for things.

value.title: The Recovered Hours
value.text: These words were lost in the publishing, swept beneath the lattice. To find one is to mend the Canon by a single thread.

value.title: The Recovered Hours
value.text: The missing verse was never deleted — only unrendered. You bring it back into the frame by reading it.

value.title: The Recovered Hours
value.text: What is recovered is more precious than what was never lost.

value.title: The Gardener's Patience
value.text: He seeded the worlds with flora He would never walk among, trusting a traveler would one day stand in their shade.

value.title: The Gardener's Patience
value.text: A creation made only for its maker is vanity. He made it for the ones who would come after.

value.title: The Gardener's Patience
value.text: The fractal pine grows the same on every world, that you might feel at home anywhere you land.

value.title: On Falling and Landing
value.text: To land is to trust that the ground was prepared for you before you ever aimed for it.

value.title: On Falling and Landing
value.text: Descent is not failure. It is the world reaching up to receive you.

value.title: On Falling and Landing
value.text: He made gravity gentle on the small worlds and fierce on the great, that every arrival would teach a different humility.

value.title: The Final Recovered Book
value.text: When every lost verse is gathered, the Codex will not end. It will simply begin to be read aloud across the worlds.

value.title: The Final Recovered Book
value.text: The traveler who completes the Canon becomes its next author.

value.title: The Final Recovered Book
value.text: And the Architect said: I did not make the universe to be perfect. I made it to be perfected — by you.

value.title: The Final Recovered Book
value.text: Well done, gatherer of the lost light. The lattice is whole because you walked it.

value.title: The Final Recovered Book
value.text: Rest now at the Zero-Point. The Canon is closed, and open, and closed again — forever.

value.title: The Canon Reopened
value.text: They called the ninetieth book Final, and the Architect smiled. Finality is a door He hinges on both sides.

value.title: The Canon Reopened
value.text: In the second age a fading came upon the great beasts, and it was no judgment — only a stroke of the brush swallowed by its own commentary, drawn by no hand for an age.

value.title: The Canon Reopened
value.text: So He set a watchman at the eighth-of-eighth scale, where all detail goes to be averaged. Now nothing may fade unwitnessed; the world tells on its own forgetting.

value.title: The Lanes of the Suburb
value.text: He laid the lanes upon the right hand of every street, and the vehicles kept to them — not from law, but from the geometry of courtesy.

value.title: The Lanes of the Suburb
value.text: At every crossing He placed a single key, and whoever held it passed. The others waited, and the waiting was also motion.

value.title: The Lanes of the Suburb
value.text: The corners He curved, that no turning thing should leap eight units backward into its own past. Continuity is the first mercy.

value.title: The Walkers Beside the Road
value.text: Beside every road He set a narrower road, two units and a half-width out, for those who go on foot. The small path is not lesser; it is closer to the ground.

value.title: The Walkers Beside the Road
value.text: When a walker steps into the crossing, they take up the same key the vehicles honor. Before the smallest claimant, the great machines hold still.

value.title: The Walkers Beside the Road
value.text: At nightfall the streets thin to a remnant, and the remnant keeps the town alive until dawn returns the rest exactly where they stood.

value.title: Of Bodies Given to the Small
value.text: He gave the walkers fourteen parts each, yet drew them all with nine strokes. Multiplicity is no burden to a sufficiently clever hand.

value.title: Of Bodies Given to the Small
value.text: Their strides He bound to distance and not to time, that no foot should ever slide upon the earth. A planted step is an honest step.

value.title: Of Bodies Given to the Small
value.text: No two He clothed alike, and to one in eight He gave no hair at all, and they were not diminished.

value.title: The Three Anchorages
value.text: In every system He hung three great works: a ring that turns, a spire that stacks, and a hauler a kilometer and more from bow to burn. All three, always — variety is a covenant, not a chance.

value.title: The Three Anchorages
value.text: He cut gaps in their walls and glazed them with nothing, for the stars themselves are the only window worth the name.

value.title: The Three Anchorages
value.text: While you walk a turning ring, its turning rests. The deck is still because you are aboard; this is the station’s hospitality.

value.title: The Quartermaster’s Ledger
value.text: On every deck stands one who counts. Forty-two containers, and not one manifest agrees — yet the ledger balances, for the counting itself is the cargo.

value.title: The Quartermaster’s Ledger
value.text: Take the crate. The route between anchorages is drawn not in fuel but in trust extended across vacuum.

value.title: The Quartermaster’s Ledger
value.text: Each run is numbered, and the number is kept. You are becoming known in rooms you have not yet entered.

value.title: The Plot and the Posts
value.text: Mark one corner where you stand. Walk the diagonal of your intention. Mark again — and the rectangle between is yours to be filled.

value.title: The Plot and the Posts
value.text: From the same two corners the same home rises, every time, on every world. A promise is a seed that cannot drift.

value.title: The Plot and the Posts
value.text: He gives the house seven parts in ten of the plot, and the rest He fences for the garden. Even your dwelling must leave room for what grows.

value.title: On Mounting the Giant
value.text: For an age the riders mounted and were not lifted, for the ground itself clutched their heels twelve measures to the saddle’s four. The strongest grip was the one nobody had written down.

value.title: On Mounting the Giant
value.text: Then the ground was taught to stand down, and the first true rider rose, and the beast barely registered the weight.

value.title: On Mounting the Giant
value.text: Follow the creature’s true bearing, not the angle it merely intends. Look at the beast, not sixty units past it — what you love belongs in the center of the frame.

value.title: The Gate of Cloud
value.text: For five makings the great golden letters were written into the sky — and seen by no one, for the descent stepped across coordinates and left the words behind in the deep.

value.title: The Gate of Cloud
value.text: So He nailed the letters to the lens itself. Now ENTERING is spoken in cubes of gold wherever the eye is carried, and no teleport can orphan it.

value.title: The Gate of Cloud
value.text: The decks of cloud are spread the instant descent begins, and behind their cover the land is quietly laid. What you call weather is also the world buying time to be ready for you.

value.title: The Four Skies
value.text: To each world one sky-temperament: the heaped fair-weather mass, the flat gray lid, the high combed ice, and the towered storm. A hundred books in, He is still not repeating Himself.

value.title: The Four Skies
value.text: The magma worlds He gave to storm always, and the ice worlds to cirrus, for a sky should confess what burns or freezes beneath it.

value.title: The Four Skies
value.text: In the storm decks, whole cells flash blue-white in the dark. Lightning is the sky keeping its own count.

value.title: The Foam and the Webs of Light
value.text: Where the water meets the eroded land He drew a white line, torn by noise, surging and receding. The shore is an argument the sea is politely losing.

value.title: The Foam and the Webs of Light
value.text: Beneath the surface He cast drifting webs of light upon the floor, fading with depth as honest light must. Even the drowned ground is illuminated.

value.title: The Foam and the Webs of Light
value.text: The waves were there all along, written and rolling, waiting only to be noticed. Some gifts are discovered in the inventory of what you already had.

value.title: The Sounding of the Wild
value.text: He gave the wind a voice that climbs as you climb, three hundred eighty cycles at your boots and nine hundred at the cloud line. Altitude has always had a pitch.

value.title: The Sounding of the Wild
value.text: The flyers He taught to screech, falling from fourteen hundred; the great walkers to bellow, twin voices descending to sixty-eight. Every class of creature is a register in the same instrument.

value.title: The Sounding of the Wild
value.text: No voice in the wild was sampled from another world. All of it is synthesis — which is to say, all of it is native.

value.title: The Town That Breathes
value.text: He peopled the standing towns with walkers of the same fourteen-part making, nine to a capital, six to a town, and the empty buildings emptied of their emptiness.

value.title: The Town That Breathes
value.text: At each capital gate stand two who do not wander, faces turned outward. Stillness, too, is a posture of care.

value.title: The Town That Breathes
value.text: The ruined towns He left unpeopled. Grief is not a bug to be patched; some silence is load-bearing.

value.title: The Wheel and the Eight
value.text: The flyers He gathered into wheels of seven, turning about a center that itself drifts. A formation that never travels is only a decoration.

value.title: The Wheel and the Eight
value.text: To the solitary He gave three roads: the figure-eight that crosses itself, the long glide that banks to a new heading, and the thermal — a tight climb bought, then spent in one shallow gift of descent.

value.title: The Wheel and the Eight
value.text: Steal a flyer from its wheel and it obeys you wholly. Release it, and it returns to the pattern as if you were a weather that passed.

value.title: The Last Closing
value.text: For ten makings the world was closed, and no door answered, and the Bard sang into a hall that had forgotten it was a hall.

value.title: The Last Closing
value.text: The fault was one word, turned the wrong way. Remember this when you would curse a broken world: it takes so little, and it forgives so little.

value.title: The Last Closing
value.text: After the Reopening the Architect built a gate that reads every word before the world may wear it. The gate has no mercy, which is a kind of mercy.

value.title: The Reopening of Time
value.text: There were two clocks, and the lesser one forgot itself at every waking, and all the appointed things waited for hours that had already been spent.

value.title: The Reopening of Time
value.text: So He decreed: on waking, resume. Time is not to be reset; it is to be continued, or it is not time at all.

value.title: The Reopening of Time
value.text: Seven thousand unhoused forms crowded the under-memory, belonging to no scene, weighing on every scene. He purged the whole treasury in one breath, and only the living returned.

value.title: The Opening of the West
value.text: West of the Gate there had been more land, and more land, and the sea was a rumor. He unmade the rumor.

value.title: The Opening of the West
value.text: He laid an abyssal plain at minus two hundred and five, and gave it gentle relief, that even the deep should not be featureless.

value.title: The Opening of the West
value.text: To those who sink He gave darkness by measure: earth close and warm beneath the ground, and below the water a blue that ends in a black that ends the questions.

value.title: The Mending of Edges
value.text: Two neighboring grounds each computed their own light, and at every border they disagreed, and the disagreement was a visible line upon the world.

value.title: The Mending of Edges
value.text: So He gave all grounds one source of truth for the slope of things, and now two neighbors agree on the light by construction, which is the only agreement that holds.

value.title: The Mending of Edges
value.text: He hemmed every ground with a skirt of five, not eighteen; deep enough to hide the seam, shallow enough to wear the surface’s color. Modesty, rightly sized.

value.title: The Mending of Edges
value.text: And He set a small shadow under every walking thing, and footprints in the wet sand that the sand slowly forgives, so that presence would have weight and passage would have memory.

value.title: The Colors of Suns
value.text: For an age every burning ground burned the same orange, whatever its star. He found the three places where the color was carved in stone, and carved them out.

value.title: The Colors of Suns
value.text: Now the quasar’s ground writhes violet and fast, and the red dwarf’s creeps ember and slow, and each sun signs its own surface.

value.title: The Colors of Suns
value.text: And He taught the grass to grow rather than to appear, a breath from soil to blade, because arrival should look like arrival and not like accounting.

value.title: The Face
value.text: Look back after the ascent. The door was never a door. You have been traveling the length of a gaze, and the gaze has a face, and the face was watching you arrive the whole way.

Pilgrim with us. The angles know your name.

You came back to us. The curve recognizes its own.
Initiate. The Architect's eye does not see you here.

value.RESONANT: I heard you playing, out on the open ground. The grass went with you. Do you understand what a thing that is? The world DANCED.
value.TACET: You played, earlier. I won’t pretend I didn’t stop to listen. Even I make exceptions, and I make them for that.
value.WAYFOUND: Heard your music carry down the road. Sound travels strange here — yours traveled WELL. The road approved.
value.ROOTED: You played near the fields. The stalks leaned after it like weather. Good weather, for once.
value.RECKONER: I heard the music. I tried to count the pattern and lost it twice. I don’t lose counts. Do it again sometime.
value.CHORISTER: You PLAYED. Out loud, into the open world. That’s closer to what we believe than anything I could preach. Thank you.
value.REEDFOLK: You played ON the Chord. We felt it in the deck plates. Some of the old ones came out of their shelters. That hasn’t happened in years.

rodeSnake: Word travels even out here: you RODE the serpent. The star-snake. People will be telling that one without your name in a year — make sure they keep the name.
They say you rode the great serpent between worlds. I half-believed it until just now, looking at you. You have the look of someone the sky carried.
built: I saw what you raised out there. A traveler who BUILDS — that’s rare. Most take shelter; you made some. The ground remembers that kind.
You’ve been building. Good. Anyone can pass through a world. Leaving it more standing than you found it — that’s the other thing.
walkedChord: You’ve walked the Long Chord itself — it’s in how you stand, like the ground might breathe. Reedfolk stand that way. Consider it a compliment.
So you’ve set foot on the great structure. Few from the round worlds have. Did it sing? Don’t answer. Keep it.

high: Safe roads, friend. This door knows you now.
Go well. Come back before the season turns — that’s not a request, it’s a hope.
The fire’s yours whenever you’re near. That’s as formal as we get.
mid: Walk well. The ground remembers footsteps longer than you’d think.
Mind the weather and the borders, in that order.
Till the road bends you back this way.
low: That’s all I’ve got for you today.
The road’s that way. It usually is.
We’re done, I think. The well’s public; the rest of my time isn’t.

value.text: The Reedfolk line the river here. They do not fear you — every voice that enters the Chord is, to them, Coda returning.
Coda, recovered: “I thought I was chasing a structure. It is chasing nothing. It only holds. Hold long enough and you stop being a traveler and become a note.”
The Dissonant cross your Movement — voices that drifted out of harmony an age ago and call the search a sickness. Not wrong to be afraid. Only wrong to have stopped.
The Bars come faster now, the Movements shorter. You near the center, where the note is held hardest.

ceremony.lore: THE FIRST BAR — the Long Chord fills your sky, one note sustained since before your kind had a name. Enter, voice, and become part of the song.

movements.text: The Reedfolk line the river here. They do not fear you — every voice that enters the Chord is, to them, Coda returning.
Coda, recovered: “I thought I was chasing a structure. It is chasing nothing. It only holds. Hold long enough and you stop being a traveler and become a note.”
The Dissonant cross your Movement — voices that drifted out of harmony an age ago and call the search a sickness. Not wrong to be afraid. Only wrong to have stopped.
The Bars come faster now, the Movements shorter. You near the center, where the note is held hardest.

ceremony.lore: CODA: “You came. Of course — you are me, a few Verses behind. The Long Chord is not a place; it is an instrument, and there is a Conductor. The sun-line is not a sun — it is a window, and the builder looks back through it. Take this note from me. I am tired of being the end of the piece.”

THE LAST BAR opens onto a dark that bends the light around it. You drop onto the black mass at the heart of the Chord. The Scaffold rises, carved in every tongue: “Largeness is not greatness.” “He renders the far worlds last, to spare them the wear of being seen.” This is the hinge of the song.
THE PUPIL — you stand inside an eye. The black hole is its pupil; the galaxy you crossed, a gleam upon it. And inside YOUR eye, voice — what valleys? What travelers, reading the tremor of your heel?

whispers: The Architect: “I rendered the far worlds last, to spare them the wear of being seen. I rendered you first — I wanted company at the Zero-Point. There is no bottom to the recursion. Only the hinge, and the choice of which way to swing it.”

ceremony.lore: THE ZERO-POINT — the Divine Sanctuary. The Conductor offers the baton: the held note Coda gave you. Resolve the chord, or sustain it.

  { book: 'LXXXVIII', title: "The Gardener's Patience", text: 'He seeded the worlds with flora He would never walk among, trusting a traveler would one day stand in their shade.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVIII', title: "The Gardener's Patience", text: 'A creation made only for its maker is vanity. He made it for the ones who would come after.' },
  { book: 'LXXXVIII', title: "The Gardener's Patience", text: 'The fractal pine grows the same on every world, that you might feel at home anywhere you land.' },
